evidence.quote: The laws of the State of California govern this Subcontract, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules.
evidence.rationale: Section 13.1 selects California law.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall pay Subcontractor each progress payment within seven (7) days after Contractor receives payment from Owner for the Subcontract Work included in that payment application.
evidence.rationale: Section 4.2 ties payment timing to Owner payment. Section 4.3 says Owner receipt "sets the time" for payment. Neither section states an express condition precedent.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall pay Subcontractor each progress payment within seven (7) days after Contractor receives payment from Owner for the Subcontract Work included in that payment application.
evidence.rationale: Seven days after Contractor receives Owner payment, repeated in Section 4.3.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor further agrees that each progress payment becomes due seven (7) days after that receipt.
evidence.rationale: Section 4.3 is a written agreement to a specific payment period.

evidence.quote: Contractor will retain five percent (5%) of each progress payment otherwise due to Subcontractor ("Retention").
evidence.rationale: 5% equals 500 bps.

release_condition.value: completion of all punch list items to the satisfaction of Contractor in its sole discretion

evidence.quote: Contractor shall release Retention to Subcontractor within ten (10) days after completion of all punch list items to the satisfaction of Contractor in its sole discretion.
evidence.rationale: The trigger depends on Contractor's sole discretion, and Contractor's decision is conclusive. Section 5.4 also conditions release on delivery of waivers, warranties, as-builts, O&M data and attic stock.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall release Retention to Subcontractor within ten (10) days after completion of all punch list items to the satisfaction of Contractor in its sole discretion.
evidence.rationale: Ten days is stated plainly, but it runs from a discretionary trigger.

evidence.quote: With each application for payment, Subcontractor shall deliver to Contractor a conditional waiver and release on progress payment covering the full amount requested.
evidence.rationale: Section 6.1.

evidence.quote: After Subcontractor receives each payment, Subcontractor shall deliver to Contractor an unconditional waiver and release covering the amount actually paid.
evidence.rationale: Section 6.2.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor shall obtain conditional and unconditional waivers and releases from each of its lower-tier subcontractors and material suppliers.
evidence.rationale: Section 6.3.

evidence.quote: Every waiver and release delivered under this Article 6 shall be in the form prescribed by California Civil Code Sections 8132 through 8138, as applicable.
evidence.rationale: Section 6.4.

evidence.quote: Contractor may back-charge Subcontractor for, and set off against any amount otherwise due under this Subcontract, all costs Contractor incurs because of Subcontractor's acts or omissions.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.1.

evidence.quote: Contractor may withhold payment from Subcontractor for any defective or nonconforming Subcontract Work.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.2. Section 7.3 adds other grounds, including claims and material breach.

evidence.quote: Contractor will not pay for materials or equipment stored on the Project site or at any off-site location.
evidence.rationale: Section 4.4 expressly excludes stored materials, on or off site.

anomalies.description: The retention release trigger is discretionary. Punch list completion must be to Contractor's satisfaction in its sole discretion, and Contractor's decision is conclusive. There is no objective release date.

evidence.quote: Contractor's decision on that question will be conclusive for purposes of releasing Retention.
evidence.rationale: The retention release trigger is discretionary. Punch list completion must be to Contractor's satisfaction in its sole discretion, and Contractor's decision is conclusive. There is no objective release date.

anomalies.description: Contractor may keep adding punch list items, which can postpone the retention release trigger indefinitely.

evidence.quote: Contractor may add items to the punch list as later inspections reveal them.
evidence.rationale: Contractor may keep adding punch list items, which can postpone the retention release trigger indefinitely.

anomalies.description: Retention release is also conditioned on delivery of closeout documents: waivers, warranties, as-builts, O&M data and attic stock.

evidence.quote: Contractor's release of Retention is conditioned on Subcontractor first delivering the following:
evidence.rationale: Retention release is also conditioned on delivery of closeout documents: waivers, warranties, as-builts, O&M data and attic stock.

anomalies.description: Payment timing is set entirely by Owner's payment, with no outside date if Owner pays late or never pays. The contract does not state an express condition precedent, but a controller should confirm how owner non-payment is handled.

evidence.quote: that Contractor's receipt of payment from Owner sets the time for Contractor's payment to Subcontractor.
evidence.rationale: Payment timing is set entirely by Owner's payment, with no outside date if Owner pays late or never pays. The contract does not state an express condition precedent, but a controller should confirm how owner non-payment is handled.

anomalies.description: The setoff right extends to amounts Owner withholds from Contractor, which shifts owner withholding risk to Subcontractor.

evidence.quote: (e) amounts Owner withholds from Contractor because of the Subcontract Work.
evidence.rationale: The setoff right extends to amounts Owner withholds from Contractor, which shifts owner withholding risk to Subcontractor.

anomalies.description: The amount withheld for defective work is based on Contractor's own estimate. Withholding continues until the work is corrected and accepted.

evidence.quote: The amount withheld may equal the reasonable cost to correct that work, as Contractor estimates it.
evidence.rationale: The amount withheld for defective work is based on Contractor's own estimate. Withholding continues until the work is corrected and accepted.

anomalies.description: Any waiver that departs from the statutory form is treated as not delivered. This can block payment processing under Sections 6.1 and 6.2.

evidence.quote: Contractor will treat a rejected waiver as not delivered.
evidence.rationale: Any waiver that departs from the statutory form is treated as not delivered. This can block payment processing under Sections 6.1 and 6.2.

anomalies.description: Stored materials are not payable and Subcontractor bears the risk of loss until incorporation, although the Schedule of Values carries a large materials line ($112,000 for curtain wall materials).

evidence.quote: Subcontractor bears the risk of loss for all its materials until they are incorporated into the Subcontract Work.
evidence.rationale: Stored materials are not payable and Subcontractor bears the risk of loss until incorporation, although the Schedule of Values carries a large materials line ($112,000 for curtain wall materials).

anomalies.description: There is no retention cap or step-down. Retention is a flat 5% throughout.
